analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds a paragraph in a later hunk (head lines 1293-1298, outside the two supplied text units) about PromptPieceTokenStore.lookup snapshotting all of a request's hits before promoting between two bounded generations. Nothing in the diff is executable or alters a control. The supplied units (head lines 1-805) are unchanged surrounding documentation: Nemotron Super load/admission, SSD prefix-cache checkpoints, and the cache-scope and logprobs descriptions. I found nothing there that weakens a stated mitigation. The text still states that prefix reuse is partitioned by the authenticated cache scope and off without one, that durable checkpoints are encrypted under the provider cache root, and that image requests without a scope stay cold. Those statements are consistent with T-041 (cross-tenant prefix-cache sharing and the TTFT oracle, accepted as SEC-035) and with A-001. The new paragraph describes a token-piece cache that is 'reused in the same prefix-cache scope'. If the implementation is correct, snapshotting hits before promotion does not widen cross-scope sharing. This is only a documented behavior change, not verified code, because the Swift source for PromptPieceTokenStore was not supplied. Remaining integration question: whether PromptPieceTokenStore's generations are keyed by cache scope in code, so the snapshot and shared token-array storage cannot leak across tenants. The patch gives no evidence of a regression. This is a documentation-only change and needs no deeper security review beyond that check.
